_comment: Applications ZUZZ may open without an extra prompt. The key is what the
user types; the value is what gets launched. An app that is NOT here can
still be opened, but it is mapped to run_safe_commands and so asks at every
trust level rather than auto-approving like the entries below.
This file is re-read on every lookup, so an edit takes effect without a restart.
The whitelist is a convenience, not a security boundary: it removes prompts, it
does not grant access. An application that is not here is still launchable, it
just asks every time.
Removing an entry does not block that app, it only removes the auto-approval.
WHERE AN EXECUTABLE LIVES: the values below are names, not paths, and that is
deliberate. body.hands.app_registry.locate() resolves each one in this order:
1. the user's PATH, so System32 entries like notepad.exe stay bare names;
2. KNOWN_APP_PATHS in body/hands/app_registry.py, which lists where Chrome,
Firefox, Edge, VS Code, Brave, Opera, Slack, Discord, Spotify and Office
actually install - the Chrome, Firefox and Edge installers deliberately do
not add themselves to PATH, so without this table 'Open Chrome' resolved to
a name that cannot be launched;
3. the name unchanged, so the launch fails with an accurate error rather than
ZUZZ asserting an application it simply could not find does not exist.
Add an application here if you want it to auto-approve. If its installer does
not use PATH, also add its location to KNOWN_APP_PATHS.
